outcome: Only permanents are offered as legal targets unless the spell or ability names another zone or players, as shown in the legal target list.
The same object is not offered twice for one instance of the word target but may fill separate instances.
Any target offers only creatures, players, planeswalkers and battles as legal targets.
A spell or ability on the stack is not among its own legal targets.
A target change succeeds only if every changed target moves to another legal target; otherwise all targets stay as they were.
Changing a target alters at most one target and only to another legal target, else nothing changes.
Changing any targets alters any number of targets, each only to another legal target.
Choosing new targets leaves unchanged targets in place even if illegal, and changed targets must be legal.
Swapping targets between two target slots is allowed because only the final target set is checked.
A retargeted divided effect keeps its original division among the targets.
Retargeting a modal spell keeps its chosen modes and only changes targets within each mode.
A trigger checking a spell or ability with a number of targets counts targets chosen when it was put on the stack, regardless of current legality.
A trigger checking what a spell or ability targets uses the targets' current state, and ignores targets that left their zone.
A trigger checking a spell that targets only something counts distinct targets chosen, then checks that one target's current state.
